chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Qasāmah was only instituted so that severity may be imposed thereby upon a man known for evil and under suspicion. If they testify against him, their testimony is accepted."

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ الْمَعْرُوفِ بِالشَّرِّ: a man known for evil or wicked conduct
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةُ: the collective oath procedure used in a legal case, especially in homicide-related accusation
key_terms.الْمُتَّهَمِ: the one under accusation or suspicion
key_terms.لِيُغَلَّظَ: to impose severity or intensify legal pressure

ai.seo_question: Why was qasāmah instituted in cases involving a suspected person known for evil?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal rationale of qasāmah as a measure used in the case of a person known for wickedness and placed under suspicion. It indicates the acceptance of testimony against such a person within this judicial context, showing its place in Islamic legal procedure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5178 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurarah from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"The practice of Qasamah (the collective oath) was established to impose severity upon a man known for evil and who is suspected. If they testify against him, their testimony is accepted."
